item.title: China’s Leader Xi Seeks to Extend Truce with Trump During U.S. Summit
item.description: Facing an American president constrained by war and politics, China’s leader may seek to lock in a tactical truce while he shores up a fragile economy at home.
item.dc:creator: David Pierson
item.media:description: President Trump and the Chinese leader, Xi Jinping, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing in May.

item.title: China’s Continued Control of Rare Earths Looms Over Trump-Xi Meeting
item.description: Manufacturers are struggling with constrained supplies as U.S. and Chinese officials negotiate over export restrictions with consequences for global industry.
item.dc:creator: Keith Bradsher
item.media:description: A display about rare-earth production at the National Museum in Beijing.

item.title: Japan Meets With Trump, Hoping to Get His Help on China
item.description: Japan’s prime minister will meet President Trump to discuss China’s economic and security pressure while also seeking to de-escalate tensions with Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Javier C. Hernández and Lily Kuo
item.media:description: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi of Japan in a meeting with President Trump, who is not pictured, in Tokyo last year. Ms. Takaichi remains focused on persuading Mr. Trump to maintain security commitments in East Asia.

item.title: Why Xi Is Coming to Washington, and White House TV Feeds Go Dark
item.description: Plus, the man who helped put bugs on the menu.
item.dc:creator: Tracy Mumford, Will Jarvis, Margaret Kadifa, Jake Lucas, Ian Stewart and David Pierson

item.title: How Trump Has Cracked Down on Dissent Since the Killing of Charlie Kirk
item.description: The White House has labeled critics terrorists, attributed violence to a left-wing conspiracy and investigated unions, nonprofits and other groups in a battle over free speech.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Purdy and Alan Feuer
item.media:credit: Adriana Zehbrauskas for The New York Times
item.media:description: A memorial to Charlie Kirk outside the Turning Point USA headquarters last year in Phoenix.

item.title: Will Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez Run for President in 2028? Here’s What She Said.
item.description: In a wide-ranging interview, the New York congresswoman offered her most detailed insight yet into how she is thinking about a possible presidential run.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher
item.media:credit: Gordon Welters for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York has several choices ahead of 2028: Keep her House seat, run for the Senate or seek the White House.

item.title: Many Democrats Are Avoiding Kamala Harris. Abdul El-Sayed Is Welcoming Her.
item.description: The former vice president wants to help her party in the midterms, but not many are taking her up on the offer. Except for the Senate nominee in Michigan, who will appear with her on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Former Vice President Kamala Harris has not revealed whether she plans to run for president again in 2028, but she has taken steps to maintain her influence in the Democratic Party.

item.title: ‘I Was Sold a Bill of Goods’: Americans and the Distrust Election
item.description: Americans have a pervasive sense they are being lied to. That has created an unpredictability in politics unseen since Donald Trump said he could shoot someone on Fifth Avenue without losing voters.
item.dc:creator: Sabrina Tavernise and Lauren Lancaster
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Lauren Lancaster for The New York Times
item.media:description: The fight against a data center in Archbald, Pa., has united Democrats and Republicans, and turned voters against leaders in both parties.

item.title: George W. Bush and Cornyn Leave Out Paxton as They Raise Cash for Senate Candidates
item.description: The former president and Texas senator are headlining a fund-raiser in Dallas for top Republican Senate candidates. Not included: Ken Paxton, the nominee in their own state.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Kenny Holston/The New York Times; Hiroko Masuike/The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator John Cornyn of Texas, left, lost a costly and bitter Republican primary this year to Ken Paxton, the state attorney general, right. Former President George W. Bush, center, has mostly stayed out of the fray, but his politics align more with Mr. Cornyn’s.

item.title: Trump Faces the Sting of a Media Boycott After Press Pool Withdrawal
item.description: A boycott of the White House press pool by the major networks deprives the president of the oxygen of screen time. But he is still finding ways to get on the air.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker
item.media:credit: Pete Marovich for The New York Times
item.media:description: Television is how President Trump’s allies and even his aides communicate with him.

item.title: New Hope for Diagnosing C.T.E. in Brain Injured Patients
item.description: Scientists are developing imaging techniques and blood tests that one day may enable doctors to identify the disease definitively in living patients.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Jacobs
item.media:description: Hundreds of people, most of them professional football players, have been diagnosed with C.T.E., or chronic traumatic encephalopathy, which is associated with repeated impacts to the head, in recent years.

item.title: The ‘Kid’ Takes Over: David Ellison Becomes a Hollywood Colossus
item.description: With Paramount and Warner Bros. under his control, Mr. Ellison will be “the Hollywood equivalent of Superman, Caesar and Midas combined.” But challenges remain.
item.dc:creator: Brooks Barnes
item.media:description: David Ellison, the 43-year-old chief executive of Paramount Skydance, will run an empire of unprecedented breadth in Hollywood.

item.title: What’s Next for Paramount
item.description: Hollywood watchers believe the studio prevailed over states seeking to block its deal for Warner Bros. Discovery. It’s now free to reshape the media industry.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe and Sri Muppidi
item.media:description: Paramount is now free to complete its planned takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, a deal that could reshape Hollywood.

item.title: The Big Threat Has Been Climate Change. Now Comes A.I.
item.description: Both are human-caused, both are frightening, and one of them has raced to the forefront of the global conversation.
item.dc:creator: Chico Harlan
item.media:description: Construction of an A.I. data center in Texas last month.

item.title: What to Know About Recent A.I. Hacks
item.description: OpenAI, Google and others recently disclosed breaches by their artificial intelligence models that amplified concerns about the advancing capabilities of the technology.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: An analysis of one recent hack by OpenAI technology helped to reveal how A.I. agents communicated with one another.

item.title: Earl Spencer Book Blasts Diana’s Treatment by UK Royal Family
item.description: The decades have not lessened Earl Spencer’s anger over the House of Windsor’s treatment of the former Princess of Wales. King Charles comes in for special vitriol.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Lyall
item.media:description: Earl Spencer, during an interview with the BBC this month. His new book, “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister,” comes out on Tuesday.

item.title: Book Review: “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister,” by Charles Spencer
item.description: “Swan Song,” Charles Spencer’s memoir of Lady Diana, is full of love and vengeance.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Jacobs

item.media:description: Princess Diana

item.title: Takeaways From Charles Spencer’s Memoir, “Swan Song,” About Princess Diana
item.description: Nearly 30 years after Princess Diana died, her brother has written a book about her life, her marriage to Prince Charles and the suffering she endured at the hands of the tabloid press.
item.dc:creator: The Book Review

item.title: Videos Reveal New Details About ICE Shooting in Austin
item.description: A video analysis finds that a federal immigration officer was standing to the side of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez’s car when the officer apparently fired through the rear passenger window. But the events surrounding the shooting remain murky.
item.dc:creator: Devon Lum, Ainara Tiefenthäler, Robin Stein, Aric Toler and Allison McCann

item.title: Man Shot by ICE Agent Says His Car Was Struck Twice Before He Was Shot
item.description: A Venezuelan immigrant, Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, was shot in Austin, Texas, on Sunday after a traffic stop. The shooting prompted calls from local officials for a transparent investigation.
item.dc:creator: Christina Morales, Hamed Aleaziz and Billy Witz
item.media:description: Police tape surrounds the location where local authorities say a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot and wounded a man in Austin, Texas, on Sunday.

item.title: German Leaders Prepare to Deny Far Right Access to Secret War Plan
item.description: With the Alternative for Germany party close to power in a German state, federal officials are planning to limit the group’s access to classified intelligence.

item.media:description: The State Parliament in Saxony-Anhalt, a state in eastern Germany where the AfD could soon take power.
